description: `system` (standing instructions), `user` (the request), `assistant` (earlier model turns) and `tool` (tool results). The model is stateless: each call resends the conversation.
Why the output ended: `stop` (finished), `length` (cut at `maxTokens` or the context limit), `tool_calls`, `refusal` or `content_filter`.
A hard cap on output tokens. It bounds cost and latency; it does not make the model plan a shorter answer, it cuts it off.
The provider's count of input and output tokens (and cost) for one call. The number you bill, budget and alert on.
A thin function of your own between the code and the provider SDK: one place for message building, result mapping, retries, logging and test doubles.
The answer delivered as text deltas followed by a final event with finish reason and usage. Lowers time to first token, not total time.
Latency until the first output token arrives. What users perceive in a chat UI; streaming improves it.
